title: Introduction
subtitle: What is the Rapture?

pretrib.summary: The rapture is a literal catching away of the church before the final Tribulation.
pretrib.teaching: Pre-tribulation Christians understand the rapture as a distinct event in which Christ comes for His church. The dead in Christ are raised, living believers are transformed, and both are caught up to meet Jesus in the air before the Tribulation.

support.why: The words 'caught up' are read as the church being removed from the earth to meet Christ.
Jesus' promise to receive believers to Himself is connected with the rapture.

adventist.summary: The catching up happens at Christ's one visible, glorious Second Coming.
adventist.teaching: Seventh-day Adventists understand the resurrection, transformation of the living righteous, and catching up to happen together when Christ returns visibly.

support.why: The passage includes the shout, archangel, trumpet, resurrection, and gathering in one event.
Christ's return is described as visible to every eye.

bible_first: The catching up is explicit. The main question is whether it is a separate pre-tribulation event or part of the visible Second Coming.

title: Is the Rapture Secret?
subtitle: 1 Thessalonians 4:16-17

pretrib.summary: Pre-trib believers emphasize a sudden, unexpected removal of the church before the Tribulation.
pretrib.teaching: The phrase 'secret rapture' normally refers to the world not expecting the event and believers being suddenly removed. Not every pre-tribulation teacher means that the event itself is literally silent.

support.why: The Day of the Lord comes like a thief in the night, emphasizing surprise.
The unknown day and hour and the one-taken/one-left language are used to support sudden removal.

adventist.summary: Adventists reject a secret Second Coming and emphasize a public, audible, and visible return.
adventist.teaching: The shout, voice of the archangel, trumpet, resurrection, and 'every eye shall see him' are understood as a public event.

support.why: The passage explicitly includes loud, public elements.

bible_first: Suddenness is explicit. Invisibility is not stated in 1 Thessalonians 4.

title: When Does It Happen?
subtitle: Before, during or after the Tribulation?

pretrib.summary: The church is removed before the Tribulation.
pretrib.teaching: Pre-tribulation theology places the rapture before the final period of tribulation and divine judgment.

support.why: Believers are not appointed to wrath.
'Keep thee from the hour' is interpreted as removal from the coming worldwide test.

adventist.summary: God's people pass through the final crisis and are gathered when Christ returns.
adventist.teaching: Adventists distinguish tribulation from divine wrath and understand God as preserving His people through the final crisis.

support.why: The gathering of the elect is placed after the tribulation.
God's people are present during the time of trouble and are delivered.

bible_first: Matthew 24 explicitly places a gathering after tribulation. Pre-tribulation theology distinguishes that gathering from the church's earlier rapture.

title: One Taken, One Left
subtitle: Matthew 24:40-41

pretrib.summary: The one taken is often understood as a believer removed in the rapture.
pretrib.teaching: The sudden separation of two people in ordinary life is read as a picture of believers being taken while unbelievers remain.

support.why: One is taken and the other left.

adventist.summary: The Noah context is emphasized: the flood took the wicked away while Noah remained.
adventist.teaching: Adventists argue that the immediate comparison with Noah makes it unsafe to assume that being 'taken' automatically means being raptured to heaven.

support.why: The flood 'took them all away,' referring to the wicked.

bible_first: The main point is readiness because the hour is unknown. The Noah context makes this text less decisive as a stand-alone proof of a pre-tribulation rapture.

title: Differences in Timeline
subtitle: Side-by-side comparison

pretrib.teaching: The rapture and visible Second Coming are understood as two distinct stages separated by the Tribulation.

support.why: Often assigned to the later visible return.

adventist.summary: Final crisis → Visible Second Coming → Resurrection/Gathering → Millennium.
adventist.teaching: The catching up is part of Christ's one visible Second Coming.

support.why: Visible return, trumpet, and gathering occur together.
Resurrection and catching up occur together.

bible_first: The biblical passages must be compared to determine whether they describe one event or two separate stages.
